analysis.title: Stocks Slide From All Time High As Gaping Cracks Form Just Below The Surface
key_insights: US stocks slid from record highs on Oct 8, 2026 as elevated oil prices raised concern that inflation could force more Fed rate hikes. The SPX intraday range was only 43bps, but internals were weak.

Korea's Kospi fell to session lows because the 55 trillion won buyback quota used by Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix is ending sooner than expected (previously mid-November). The buybacks had propped up the Korean market for two months.

European banks plunged and French bonds sold off again. The France-Germany 10Y spread returned to 140bps as the Le Pen 'shadow budget' optimism faded and the ECB signaled French bond stress is not enough to restart bond buying.

The 10Y Treasury auction priced at 5.300%, the highest yield since November 2000, but stopped through the when-issued by 1.7bps, the biggest stop-through in over a year. The 10Y yield fell 5bps to a session low of 5.27% after hitting a multi-decade high of 5.36% earlier.
US equity futures reversed higher as Europe closed and got a further lift from the strong 10Y auction.
The NY Fed survey showed 1-year inflation expectations rose to 3.9% from 3.6%, a three-year high.

FOMC minutes were hawkish: 'most' officials assumed at least one more rate hike before year-end, and several cited the AI buildout as a source of inflation through core goods prices, energy and input costs, wages for skilled workers, and demand outpacing supply over the medium term.

Market breadth is narrow. The Russell 2000 underperformed the NDX for a fourth straight day (17 of the last 20 sessions) as small caps absorb the rate pressure. The RSP/SPY equal-weight ratio hit a new all-time low, though there were more 52-week highs than lows for a second day.

Defensive sectors led: Healthcare, Staples and Utilities outperformed. Goldman's Most Short basket fell 130bps while the Quality pair rose, which the author reads as the market starting to reward healthy balance sheets.
Goldman's high-beta thematic baskets fell sharply: Rare Earths -5.5%, Uranium -3.5%, Robotics -3%, and the PowerUp America basket -2% after its third best day in five years.

Goldman's desk reported a one-way sell day. Flow was 9% better for sale, long-only was 25% better for sale (heavy sell skew in Macro Products and Tech), hedge funds were 8% better for sale, and the hedge fund short ratio was the highest in two weeks.

Credit stress is building outside the index. Paramount CDS hit its widest since the Global Financial Crisis after a Fitch downgrade, SpaceX bonds hit all-time lows on a report of another $40B issue through an Apollo-led SPV, and Oracle bond yields hit an all-time high after its Wisconsin Project Lighthouse data center was reported delayed.
Meta's Project Beignet, the largest single corporate bond and a proxy for data center debt, fell to a new all-time low.
Crypto sold off all day, with a large drop at 10pm ET overnight and a failed recovery attempt.

The diesel crack spread rose to a two-week high despite the emergency release of 50 million barrels of diesel last week. Tanker rates are adding $40 or more per barrel, and Dated Brent reached $130, about $30 above Brent futures, reflecting scarce physical crude.
Financials kick off Q3 earnings next Tuesday with JPM, C and WFC reporting before the open.

Goldman's chart of the day: the Consumer Experiences basket (GSXUCEXP) has lagged despite spending on experiences growing 6% in Q1 2026 versus 2% for broader services. Goldman expects its currently negative correlation with AI to turn more positive.

sector_views.rationale: These sectors outperformed in a defensive rotation as rates and oil pressured the market.

Goldman notes experiences spending growth accelerated from 1% in Q1 2025 to 6% in Q1 2026 versus 2% for broader services, and higher-income exposure insulates the basket if oil stays high or de-escalation occurs.
European banks plunged as the French bond selloff revived the sovereign-bank 'doom loop' concern.
The Russell has lagged the NDX in 17 of the last 20 sessions as higher rates weigh on small caps.

earnings_insights: Financials Q3 earnings begin Tuesday (Oct 13, 2026) with JPM, C and WFC reporting before the open. No estimates are given in the note.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Highest auction yield since November 2000, but demand was strong, with a 1.7bps stop-through and the biggest stop-through in over a year. This eased concern about a weak auction.
The yield hit a new multi-decade high before falling 5bps after the auction.
A three-year high, which adds to the case for further rate hikes.

macro_indicators.reading: 'most' officials assumed at least one more rate hike before year-end
macro_indicators.interpretation: Hawkish. The minutes link the AI buildout to higher core goods inflation, wages and medium-term demand pressure.
French bond stress returned and drove the sell-off in European banks.
About $10 below its all-time high and about $30 above Brent futures, showing physical crude scarcity.

crypto_views: Crypto sold off all day, with a drop at exactly 10pm ET overnight and a failed recovery attempt. The author contrasts this with stocks, which recovered intraday.

trade_ideas.description: Buy the GS Consumer Experiences basket (GSXUCEXP) versus the AI-heavy index
trade_ideas.rationale: The basket has lagged the S&P ex-AI index despite faster experiences spending growth, and Goldman expects its correlation with AI to turn more positive.

risk_factors: Further Fed rate hikes if oil and AI buildout inflation persist.
Weak or tailing 10Y auctions with yields at the highest since 2000.
French sovereign stress spreading to European banks.
Credit stress in AI and data center debt (Oracle, Meta, SpaceX) and Paramount.
Narrow market leadership with tech carrying the index.
Elevated diesel and physical crude prices passing through to inflation.
vol_and_positioning: The SPX intraday range was only 43bps, while the rotation underneath was more extreme.
Goldman's Most Short basket fell 130bps and the Quality pair rose, with the Most Short pair at a 2+ month low.
Goldman's hedge fund short ratio is at its highest in two weeks, and hedge funds were 8% better for sale.
Long-only flow was 25% better for sale, with heavy sell skews in Macro Products and Tech.
The RSP/SPY ratio hit an all-time low.
geopolitical: The article says there was no geopolitical news to explain the decline in oil prices on the day.
Le Pen's 'shadow budget' and ECB comments on French bonds drove European sovereign stress.

tension_points.bull_case: The strong 10Y auction (1.7bps stop-through) and a gradual fall in oil helped yields and let US futures recover. Tech keeps carrying the index and there were more 52-week highs than lows for a second day.
tension_points.bear_case: Hawkish FOMC minutes pointing to another hike, 1-year inflation expectations at 3.9%, a 10Y yield around 5.3%, record-low equal-weight/cap-weight ratio, and credit stress in Oracle, Meta, SpaceX and Paramount debt.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further rise in the 10Y yield above the 5.36% high or a weak auction would undermine the bull case.
